title: Durable agentProvider is written by the operator command and read through a store port
description:
SPIDR grandchild C of task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild B (set after B is filed) so the kind is already on the registry.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the durable store (copy the environment-store event-commit shape, without encryption — this value is not a secret), a closed refusal factory (AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN plus any store-layer codes), swapping B's fail-closed registry handler for the real one, composition of the store port. New files under apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/ or apps/daemon/src/settings/.

NOT IN SCOPE: RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, MCP fence, spawn argv, pause bookkeeping, /sessions/read, UI.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.

Copy: apps/daemon/src/environment/environment-store.ts commitEnvironmentEvent; KNOWN_PROVIDERS at apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts:34.
definitionOfDone: A durable per-project `agentProvider` (claude|codex) with a per-goal override is written by `project.set_agent_provider` and read back. goalId "" is the project default; a non-empty goalId is the override. A read with no write returns the default `claude`. Assert the stored provider, not an in-memory field.

An unknown provider name is refused: assert code AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN AND its layer. The accepted names are taken from KNOWN_PROVIDERS (health-read.ts:34) — a test that mutates production to accept a third name without changing that roster goes RED.
The registry entry is the real store handler, not the fail-closed stub. A well-formed operator dispatch persists; a second read (new store instance against the same sqlite) returns what was written.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: REUSE KNOWN_PROVIDERS (health-read.ts:34). Import it. Do not declare a second list of provider names. Do not move the constant (that would touch health-read.ts, a concurrent-risk file).
Unknown provider refuses with a stable code AND layer (AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN). Valid names are exactly KNOWN_PROVIDERS.
Replace grandchild B's fail-closed handler; do not leave both. Unconfigured-daemon tests stay in B.
New production modules need a one-line .js bridge (copy environment-store.js). Target <=250 lines per production file; agent-spawner.ts is already 438 — do not grow it here.
FEATURES ONLY. No spawn, no /sessions/read, no UI, no MCP fence files.

THE DURABLE STORE (DoD 1). Create `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-store.ts` (+ a one-line `.js` bridge - copy the `environment-store.js` form, per rail 4).

SHAPE: a per-project `agentProvider` with a per-goal override. `goalId: ""` IS THE PROJECT DEFAULT; a non-empty goalId is that goal's override. A read with no write returns the default `claude` (DoD 1).
Make that convention explicit in the code rather than implicit in a key format - an empty string carrying "project default" is the kind of thing a later reader inverts. Say in a comment why the empty string was chosen over a nullable field.

PROVIDER NAMES COME FROM `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` (health-read.ts:34), IMPORTED (rail 1). Do not declare a second list and do not move the constant. DoD 2's arm exists precisely so that a test which widens production to a third name without changing that roster goes RED.

REFUSE `AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN` with its LAYER for an unrecognised name, using a rostered layer LITERAL (`DURABLE_STORE` for a store-layer refusal, `DAEMON_COMPOSITION` for a composition one - pick per where the check runs and say which). DECLARE NO EXPORTED `*_LAYER`/`*_LAYERS` CONSTANT: the security lane scans for them and three arms would red.

Keep the module at or under 250 lines (rail 4), and do NOT grow agent-spawner.ts, which is already 438.

REPLACE THE FAIL-CLOSED HANDLER (DoD 3). Edit `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-command.ts` and register the real store handler in `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts`.

REPLACE, DO NOT COEXIST (rail 3). Grandchild B's stub refuses `AGENT_PROVIDER_UNCONFIGURED` at :11; after this row a well-formed OPERATOR dispatch PERSISTS. Two handlers for one kind is a dispatch ambiguity and the registry sweep would then assert against whichever wins.

WHAT STAYS IN GRANDCHILD B (rail 3, and the governor's instruction): the ABSENT-CONFIG arm and the NON-OPERATOR AUTHORIZATION arm are unit-level and stay where they are. A daemon composed WITHOUT the provider store must still refuse `AGENT_PROVIDER_UNCONFIGURED@DAEMON_COMPOSITION` - this row makes the CONFIGURED path durable, it does not remove the unconfigured one.

REUSE THE LITERALS ALREADY IN THIS FILE. `"DAEMON_COMPOSITION"` is at :11; add no exported layer constant.

The registry edit is the entry only - `daemon-command-registry.ts` was 449 lines and past the 400 cap at the merge-base, so add nothing else to it and disclose that measurement in the completion record.

TRANSITION THE COMPOSED ARM TO DURABILITY (the governor's instruction (b)) - `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.test.ts`.

THE ARM AT :530-536 currently proves the stub: a valid operator payload `{ base: "main", goalId: "", provider: "codex" }` refuses and writes NOTHING, verified by a `snapshot()` over `decisionCount(reader)` and `reader.readEventHorizon()`. AFTER THIS ROW A VALID COMPOSED DISPATCH MUST PERSIST.
CHANGE WHAT IT ASSERTS; DO NOT DELETE IT. Keep the snapshot technique - it is how "no writes" was proven and it is exactly how "EXACTLY ONE write" should be. Assert the decision count and event horizon MOVE by the expected amount, not merely that something changed: a handler that writes twice passes a "changed" assertion.

LEAVE THE OTHER TWO PINS GREEN:
- :255-257, the empty-payload sweep reaching `PREREQUISITE`. Its comment says the empty payload it sends is the CORRECT one for that row; if your change makes it red, you have altered the prerequisite gate rather than the handler.
- :1119-1129, the three-axis operator fence. Its "THE SUBJECT IS ACTUALLY SERVED" guard exists because every axis would pass vacuously for an unserved kind - replacing the stub with a real handler must keep this GREEN, and if it trips, the registration is wrong.

Re-read HEAD before editing: this file is contended by several rows.

THE STORE'S OWN ARMS (DoD 1, 2, 3) - `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-store.test.ts`.

(a) DEFAULT AND OVERRIDE: `goalId: ""` writes the project default; a non-empty goalId writes that goal's override; a read for a goal with no override falls back to the project default; a read with NO write at all returns `claude` (DoD 1). Four distinct reads, because the fallback chain is where an off-by-one in key handling hides.
(b) DURABILITY ACROSS INSTANCES (DoD 3): write, then open a NEW `SqliteEventStore` against the SAME sqlite path and read back. An in-memory read proves the object, not the store - and DoD 3 names a second instance specifically.
(c) UNKNOWN PROVIDER (DoD 2): refuses `AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN` with its LAYER. Never merely that it failed.
(d) THE `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` COUPLING (DoD 2's real point): assert the accepted set EQUALS the imported `KNOWN_PROVIDERS`, so widening production to a third name without changing that roster goes RED. Import the constant and compare - do not re-spell the two names, which would make the arm agree with a copy rather than the source.
(e) An override for a goal does not disturb the project default, and vice versa.

DECLARE NO EXPORTED CONSTANT matching the security scan in the test file either - the scan reads source, not just production modules.

GATES - each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:

If it reds on a roster or cardinality arm, you declared a scanned constant - remove it rather than rostering it, because rostering owes BEFORE/AFTER/RACE coverage (completeness.security.ts:300-307) that is not this row's.
